newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Students gather in Kinshasa despite protest ban.
newsitem.headline: Students gather in Kinshasa despite protest ban.

text.p: Dozens of students wearing white bandanas gathered outside their college in Kinshasa on Wednesday, stopping cars and demanding money for the burial of a student killed in protests the previous day, witnesses said.

The government, anxious to head off a witchhunt of ethnic Tutsis in the capital over a Tutsi revolt in eastern Zaire and charges of involvement by Tutsi-led Rwanda, has banned all protests indefinitely.
Several thousand students defied the ban on Tuesday to demand the resignation of part-Tutsi prime minister, Kengo wa Dondo. Students said a colonel shot dead one of their number.
"There was one woman wounded and one student killed in the demonstration yesterday," Zairean television journalist Roger Koy told Reuters on on Wednesday, adding:
"Students were already gathering at the institute of commerce at 8 a.m. They are organising a collection for their comrade... They are stopping cars and asking for money."
Students told Reuters they planned to march from the train station to the town centre.
An estimated 1,000 Tutsis have fled by boat across the Zaire River to Brazzaville, capital of neighbouring Congo. Some reported attempts by Zaireans to tip them overboard.
Mobs have attacked Tutsi-owned property in Kinshasa.
